paragraphs: Logistic Properties of the Americas was incorporated as an exempted company with limited liability under the laws of the Cayman Islands on October 9, 2023. The mailing address of the Company's registered office is c/o Conyers Trust Company (Cayman) Limited, Cricket Square, Hutchins Drive, P.O. Box 2681, Grand Cayman, KY1-1111, Cayman Islands and its telephone number is +506 2204-7020. The Company's principal executive office address is 1395 Brickell Avenue, Suite 800, Miami, FL 33131 and its chief administrative office is located at Plaza Tempo, Edificio B, Oficina B1, Piso 2, San Rafael de Escazú, San José, Costa Rica.

Prior to the consummation of the Business Combination, LPA's business was operated by LatAm Logistic Properties, S.A., a C-corporation organized under the laws of the Republic of Panama ("LLP"). LLP was originally incorporated as a limited liability company, as provided in Law. No 4 of 2009 by Public Deed No. 6409 dated April 29, 2015, and registered before the Public Registry of Panama on May 4, 2015. On January 13, 2021, LLP was converted into a C-corporation regulated by Law No. 32 of 1927, with resolution duly registered before the Public Registry of Panama on January 13, 2021.

On March 27, 2024, LPA consummated the Business Combination (the "Business Combination") pursuant to the Business Combination Agreement (the "Business Combination Agreement") by and among two, a Cayman Islands exempted company ("TWOA"), LLP and, by joinder agreements, each of LPA, Logistic Properties of the Americas Subco, a Cayman Islands exempted company and a wholly-owned subsidiary of LPA ("SPAC Merger Sub"), and LPA Panama Group Corp., a company incorporated under the laws of Panama and a wholly-owned subsidiary of LPA ("Company Merger Sub"). As a result, on March 27, 2024: (i) SPAC Merger Sub merged with and into TWOA, with TWOA surviving the merger (the "SPAC Merger") and, in connection therewith, each issued and outstanding security of TWOA

immediately prior to the effective time of the Mergers (as defined below) (the "Effective Time") was automatically canceled and deemed no longer outstanding, in exchange for the right of each holder thereof to receive a substantially equivalent security amount of Ordinary Shares of the Company; (ii) Company Merger Sub, merged with and into LLP, with LLP surviving the merger (the "Company Merger," and together with the SPAC Merger, the "Mergers") and, in connection therewith, each issued and outstanding security of LLP immediately prior to the Effective Time was automatically cancelled and deemed no longer outstanding, in exchange for the right of each holder thereof to receive Ordinary Shares; and (iii) as a result of the Mergers, TWOA and LLP each became wholly-owned subsidiaries of LPA, and the Ordinary Shares were listed on the NYSE American.

In connection with the Business Combination, on February 16, 2024, TWOA entered into the PIPE Subscription Agreement with Bonaventure Investments Holding Inc. (such investor and its permitted successors and assigns, the "PIPE Subscriber"), pursuant to which the PIPE Subscriber purchased 1,500,000 TWOA Class A ordinary shares (the "PIPE Shares") at a price of $10.00 per share, for an aggregate purchase price of $15,000,000, in a private placement (the "PIPE Investment") that was consummated at the Effective Time. The PIPE Shares were converted into 1,500,000 Ordinary Shares in connection with the Mergers. In connection with the PIPE Investment, the PIPE Subscriber was granted certain registration rights.

Our goal is to be the leading developer, owner and manager of logistics and industrial facilities of the future across Latin America. Our mission is to provide logistics and industrial real estate solutions that enable the most efficient distribution of goods for a more environmentally conscious society.

We are a fully integrated, internally managed real estate company that develops, owns and manages a diversified portfolio of warehouse logistics and industrial assets across Latin America. We focus on modern logistics and industrial Class A Real Estate in high growth and high barrier-to-entry markets that are undersupplied and have low penetration rates. We believe we are a leading institutional, development, logistics and industrial platform in our four countries of operation today: Costa Rica, Colombia, Peru, and Mexico. We have significant expertise in designing and developing logistics and industrial assets, which we own, manage and lease on a long-term basis. Our strategic footprint and operational expertise enable us to provide our tenants with "last mile" distribution capabilities that are critical to logistics and industrial infrastructure and be well located to leverage strong e-Commerce and "nearshoring" trends.

Our business model is designed to generate recurring revenue from long-term leases with creditworthy tenants, which we believe drives attractive unit economics. We believe our corporate structure provides us with the following advantages:

•Investment focus: We have designed our business model to participate across the real estate value creation chain including (i) structuring and financing, (ii) development, (iii) lease-up and (iv) asset management, in comparison to REITs, which are generally required to focus on Stabilized Properties or nearly Stabilized Properties;

•Management fee structure: We manage our properties internally and do not pay management fees to third parties, which we believe better aligns our interests with investors, as opposed to the externally managed REIT model; and

•Long term value creation: We develop and manage our assets with a focus on the quality of our real estate and maximizing its long-term value, in comparison to managing our development, operations and maintenance activities to achieve shorter term dividend targets.

headings: Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry
Interest rate fluctuations may increase our borrowing costs and affect the valuation of our real estate portfolio, potentially impacting our financial performance and investment returns.

Our clients operate in certain specific industrial sectors in Costa Rica, Colombia, Peru, and Mexico. Thus, our business operations may be adversely affected by an economic downturn in any of these sectors.
Any increase in competition could lead to lower occupancy rates and rental income and could result in fewer investment opportunities.
We are dependent on our ability to raise capital through financial markets, divestitures, or other sources to meet our future growth expectations.
Our levels of indebtedness may affect our cash flows and expose our properties to the risk of foreclosure.
The agreements governing our existing indebtedness include financial and other covenants that impose limitations on our ability to pursue certain business opportunities or to take certain actions.
Certain provisions within our lease agreements may be deemed legally unenforceable in the jurisdictions where we operate, potentially limiting our contractual rights and remedies.
Our insurance coverage may not cover all the risks to which we may have exposure.
Our tenants may default on their obligation to maintain required insurance coverage which could expose us to uninsured property damage and liability claims.
A decrease in the fair value of our investment properties may adversely affect our results of operations.
We are subject to risks related to the development of new properties, including due to an increase in construction costs and supply chain issues.
We may fail to maintain, obtain or renew or may experience material delays in obtaining requisite governmental or other approvals, licenses and permits for the conduct of our business.
Our real estate assets may be subject to eminent domain and dispossession by the governments of the countries in which we operate for reasons of public interest and other reasons.
We may not be successful in executing our growth strategy if we are unable to make acquisitions of real estate.
We may acquire properties and companies that involve risks that could adversely affect our business and financial condition.
paragraphs: The following risk factors apply to our business and operations. These risk factors are not exhaustive, and investors are encouraged to perform their own research with respect to our business, financial condition and prospects. You should carefully consider all the following risk factors, together with all of the other information included or incorporated by reference in this Annual Report, including the financial information.

In addition to the other information contained in this Annual Report, including the matters addressed under the heading "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements," you should carefully consider the risk factors described below, which include both material and other identified risks, but are not exhaustive. Additional risks whether currently unknown or deemed immaterial, or common to businesses generally, may materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

If any of the risks outlined below materialize, whether individually or in combination, they may materially and adversely affect LPA's business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows and future outlook. This can potentially result in a decline in the market price of Ordinary Shares, and could result in a partial or total loss of your investment. Generally, investing in securities of issuers from emerging market countries, such as Costa Rica, Colombia, Peru, and Mexico, carries risks that differ from those associated with investing in securities from U.S. issuers.

Our business success significantly depends on general economic and specific market conditions within the industrial and logistics real estate industry. Any adverse changes in these conditions, including economic slowdowns or downturns in real estate asset values or leasing activity may materially and adversely affect our business operations, financial condition, results of operations and future prospects.

Our operating results and financial performance are significantly influenced by macroeconomic conditions and specific market dynamics within the industrial and logistics real estate sector. As a result, our financial and operating performance, the value of our real estate assets, our revenue stream and our ability to implement our business strategy may be affected by changes in national and regional economic conditions.

The performance of the real estate markets in which we operate tends to be cyclical and tied to the condition of the U.S. economy and the economies in the countries in which we operate, including Costa Rica, Colombia, Peru, and Mexico, as well as to investors' perceptions of the global economic outlook. Fluctuations in nominal gross domestic product ("GDP"), increased inflation, rising interest rates, declining employment levels, declining levels of investments and economic activity, declining demand for real estate, declining real estate values and periods of general economic slowdown or recession, or perceptions that any of these events may occur or are occurring, have had a negative impact on the real estate market in the past and may adversely affect our future performance. In addition, the performance of the economies of the countries in which we operate may be dependent on or driven by one or more specific industries and by other factors affecting local economies. Other factors that may affect general economic conditions or local real estate conditions include: population and demographic trends, employment and personal income trends, income and other tax laws, changes in interest rates and availability and costs of financing, increased operating costs (including insurance premiums, utilities and real estate taxes, due to inflation and other factors which may not necessarily be offset by increased rents), changes in the price of oil, construction costs and weather-related events. Our ability to reconfigure our portfolio rapidly in response to changes in economic conditions is extremely limited.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of the financial condition and results of operations should be read together with our audited consolidated financial statements as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024 and for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, together with related notes thereto (the "Audited Consolidated Financial Statements"), and the rest of our Annual Report on Form 20-F for the year ended December 31, 2025. The Audited Consolidated Financial Statements have been prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards. The following discussion contains forward-looking statements.
We generate revenue through investment property rental income and development fees.

Investment property rental income primarily consists of rental payments from tenants through operating lease agreements. Our leases with tenants (customers) are classified as operating leases. We recognize the total minimum lease payments provided for under the leases on a straight-line basis over the lease term. Rental income is recognized under the requirements of IFRS 16, Leases ("IFRS 16") and revenue on the non-lease components is recognized under the requirements of IFRS 15, Revenue from Contracts with Customers ("IFRS 15"). This is included as rental revenue in our consolidated statements of profit or loss and comprehensive income (loss).

Development fees are determined in accordance with the terms specified on each arrangement with customers. The fees are recognized as revenue when they are earned under the agreements with customers. They are included in other revenue in our consolidated statements of profit or loss and comprehensive income (loss).

Investment property operating expense includes the direct operating expenses of the property, including repairs and maintenance, property management costs, utilities, insurance, real estate taxes, expected credit loss adjustments, tenant-billable operating expenses, interest expense on property-related land lease liabilities, and other property-related expenses. The majority of the property operating expenses can be recovered through the rental recoveries charged to tenants.

General and administrative expense includes personnel costs such as salaries, bonuses, employee benefits, director fees, and share-based payments expenses; operating costs of the business support functions, including finance and accounting, legal, human resources and administrative, as well as service and professional fees, office expenses, and bank service charges.

Listing expense is recognized upon consummation of the Business Combination in accordance with IFRS 2, Share-based Payment ("IFRS 2"), representing the difference in the fair value of the shares deemed to have been issued by the accounting acquirer and the fair value of the accounting acquiree's identifiable net assets, which represents a service received by the accounting acquirer. Refer to Note 4 of the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements for further information.

Investment property valuation gain is the investment properties' change in fair value. The valuation analysis is performed by an independent external firm, which determines the fair market value of the investment properties. The fair market value of an investment property depends on the type of property. We hold operating properties, properties under development, and land.

Interest income from affiliates mainly consists of interest generated by issuing notes to related parties and key personnel. No interest income from affiliates was recognized during the year ended December 31, 2025, as the only note to related parties and key personnel outstanding was settled in March 2024.

Financing costs consist of interest expense, costs of raising debt, and amortization expense of deferred financing costs. These costs include various fees and charges associated with the process of issuing debt, refinancing the debt, and other fees and commissions paid to third parties involved in the financing process. Interest expense represents the interest costs incurred through loans.

Net foreign currency gain (loss) consists of the net profit or loss generated through the settlement of monetary items or from the remeasurement of monetary items using exchange rates that differ from those applied upon initial recognition.

Gain on sale of investment property consists of profit or loss recognized through disposal of our investment properties. The properties are carried at fair value prior to disposal. Disposals of our properties require a deduction of the cost of selling the property from the fair value price, which may result in a gain or loss on the sale.

Other income consists of interest income from certificates of deposit and bank accounts as well as installment payment receivables from the sale of investment properties, income in connection with certain lock-up release agreements that we entered into with certain non-affiliated shareholders in June 2024 (the "Lock-Up Release Agreements," "Lock-Up Shares"), and other miscellaneous income, including stamp-duty tax refunds.

Other expenses consists of transaction-related costs in connection with the Business Combination and Share Purchase Agreement, fees in connection with the Lock-Up Release Agreements, transaction costs related to the New Circle SEPA, and other miscellaneous expenses, including capital raising costs, deal pursuit costs, and loss on disposition of properties.

paragraphs: Logistic Properties of the Americas 於 2023 年 10 月 9 日根據開曼羣島法律註冊為一間有限責任豁免公司。本公司註冊辦事處的郵寄地址為 c/o Conyers Trust Company (Cayman) Limited, Cricket Square, Hutchins Drive, P.O. Box 2681, Grand Cayman, KY1-1111, Cayman Islands，電話號碼為 +506 2204-7020。本公司主要營業地址為 1395 Brickell Avenue, Suite 800, Miami, FL 33131，主要行政辦公室位於 Plaza Tempo, Edificio B, Oficina B1, Piso 2, San Rafael de Escazú, San José, Costa Rica。

在完成業務合併前，LPA 的業務由 LatAm Logistic Properties, S.A.（"LLP"）經營，LLP 是根據巴拿馬共和國法律註冊的 C 型公司。LLP 最初根據 Law. No. 4 of 2009 以 Public Deed No. 6409 日期為 2015 年 4 月 29 日的公證文註冊，並於 2015 年 5 月 4 日在巴拿馬公證處註冊。2021 年 1 月 13 日，LLP 轉為根據 Law No. 32 of 1927 規範的 C 型公司，並於 2021 年 1 月 13 日在巴拿馬公證處完成註冊。

2024 年 3 月 27 日，LPA 根據 Business Combination Agreement（"Business Combination Agreement"）完成業務合併（"Business Combination"），該協議由兩間，一間為開曼羣島豁免公司（"TWOA"）、LLP，以及經加入協議，LPA、Logistic Properties of the Americas Subco，一間為開曼羣島豁免公司且為 LPA 的 wholly-owned 子公司（"SPAC Merger Sub"），以及 LPA Panama Group Corp.，一間根據巴拿馬法律註冊的公司且為 LPA 的 wholly-owned 子公司（"Company Merger Sub"）簽訂。因此，2024 年 3 月 27 日：(i) SPAC Merger Sub 與 TWOA 合併，TWOA 繼續存續（"SPAC Merger"），並於此同時，TWOA 所有發行在外的證券

於合併生效時間（"Effective Time"）前自動註銷，並視為不再發行在外，換取持有人可獲得本公司普通股 substantially equivalent 的證券；(ii) Company Merger Sub 與 LLP 合併，LLP 繼續存續（"Company Merger"，與 SPAC Merger 合稱 "Mergers"），並於此同時，LLP 所有發行在外的證券於合併生效時間前自動註銷，並視為不再發行在外，換取持有人可獲得普通股；(iii) 由於 Mergers，TWOA 與 LLP 各成為 LPA 的 wholly-owned 子公司，普通股於紐約證券交易所美國市場（NYSE American）上市。

在完成業務合併的同時，2024 年 2 月 16 日，TWOA 與 Bonaventure Investments Holding Inc.（該投資者及其允許的繼承人與受讓人，"PIPE Subscriber"）簽訂 PIPE Subscription Agreement，PIPE Subscriber 以每股 10.00 美元的價格購入 1,500,000 TWOA 普通股（"PIPE Shares"），總購入價格為 15,000,000 美元，於合併生效時間完成私人 placements（"PIPE Investment"）。PIPE Shares 透過 Mergers 轉換為 1,500,000 普通股。在 PIPE Investment 的同時，PIPE Subscriber 獲得某些註冊權。

我們的目標是成為拉丁美洲未來物流與工業設施的領先開發者、所有者及管理者。我們的使命是提供物流與工業不動產解決方案，以實現商品最有效分佈，促進更環保的社會。

本公司為一家完全整合、 internally managed 的不動產公司，從事開發、擁有及管理橫跨拉丁美洲的多元化倉儲物流與工業資產組合。我們專注於現代物流與工業 Class A 不動產，在高成長與高進入門檻市場中，這些市場供給不足且滲透率低。我們相信，本公司目前在經營國家（哥斯大黎巴溝、哥倫比亞、祕魯與墨西哥）中，為一家領先的機構投資、開發、物流與工業平台。我們在設計與開發物流與工業資產方面擁有顯著的專業知識，這些資產由本公司擁有、管理並以長期租賃方式出租。我們的戰略佈局與運營專業知識，使我們能為租戶提供 "last mile" 分配能力，這對物流與工業基礎設施至關重要，並能處於有利位置，以利用強勁的 e-Commerce 與 "nearshoring" 趨勢。
我們的業務模式設計為透過與信用良好的租戶簽訂長期租賃契約，產生可持續的收入，我們認為這能驅動有吸引力的單位經濟效益。我們相信，本公司之公司結構為我們帶來以下優勢：
•投資重點：我們設計業務模式以參與不動產價值創造鏈，包括 (i) 結構與融資、(ii) 開發、(iii) 租賃與 (iv) 資產管理，與一般需專注於穩定不動產或近穩定不動產的 REITs 相較；
•管理費用結構：我們 internally manage 我們的不動產，並不會向第三方支付管理費用，我們認為這能更好地與投資者利益一致，與 externally managed REIT 模式相比；
•長期價值創造：我們開發與管理資產時，專注於不動產的品質與最大化其長期價值，與專注於達成較短期的股息目標之開發、運營與維護活動相比。

paragraphs: 下列對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，應與我們經審計之合併財務報表，於 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日之財務狀況，以及 2025 年、2024 年及 2023 年年度財務資料，連同相關附註（稱為「經審計之合併財務報表」），以及我們 2025 年度年報（Form 20-F）之其他內容一併閱讀。經審計之合併財務報表係依照國際會計準則（IFRS）會計準則編製。下列討論包含前瞻性陳述。
我們透過投資不動產租金收入及開發費用產生營業收入。

投資不動產租金收入主要為來自租戶（客戶）之租金付款，透過營運租賃契約。我們與租戶（客戶）之租賃契約被歸類為營運租賃。我們依照租賃契約中規定之總最低租賃付款額，於租賃期間內按直線法確認租金收入。租金收入係依照 IFRS 16，租賃（「IFRS 16」）之規定確認，而非租賃組成部分之收入則依照 IFRS 15，與客戶之契約所產生之收入（「IFRS 15」）之規定確認。此部分包含於我們合併損益及全面收益（損失）表中之租金收入。
開發費用係依照與客戶之每項安排所規定之條款確定。費用在與客戶之契約中確認為已實現時，作為收入確認。此部分包含於我們合併損益及全面收益（損失）表中之其他收入。
投資不動產營運費用包含不動產之直接營運費用，包括修繕與維護、不動產管理費用、公共設施費用、保險、不動產稅、預期信用減損調整、可向租戶計收之營運費用、與不動產相關土地租賃負債之利息費用，以及其他與不動產相關費用。不動產營運費用中絕大多數可透過向租戶計收租金予以回收。
一般及行政費用包含人資成本，如薪資、獎金、員工福利、董事費及員工持股計畫費用；以及業務支援功能之營運成本，包括財務與會計、法律、人力資源及行政，以及服務及專業費用、辦公費用及銀行服務費用。
上市費用係依照 IFRS 2，員工持股計畫（「IFRS 2」）於商業組合完成時確認，代表會計買方所發行股份之公允價值與會計被買方可辨認淨資產公允價值之間之差額，此差額代表會計買方所獲得之服務。有關進一步資訊，請參閱經審計之合併財務報表附註 4。
投資不動產評價收益為投資不動產之公允價值變動。評價分析係由獨立外部機構執行，以確定投資不動產之公允市場價值。投資不動產之公允市場價值取決於不動產類型。我們持有營運不動產、正在開發之不動產及土地。
利息收入來自聯屬公司，主要為發行債券給關聯方及關鍵人員所產生的利息。於2025年12月31日結止之會計年度內，未確認任何來自聯屬公司之利息收入，因唯一尚未償還之債券為關聯方及關鍵人員所發行，於2024年3月已償還。
融資成本包含利息支出、發行債務之成本，以及遞延融資成本之攤銷費用。這些成本包含與發行債務、重組債務以及其他與融資程序相關之第三方所支付費用及手續費。利息支出代表透過貸款所產生之利息成本。
淨外幣兌換損益為透過結算貨幣項目或因使用與初始認可時所採用匯率不同之匯率重新衡量貨幣項目而產生之淨利潤或損失。
投資性不動產出售損益為透過處置我們之投資性不動產所確認之利潤或損失。這些不動產於處置前以公允價值計入。處置這些不動產時，需從公允價值價格中扣除出售該不動產之成本，可能導致出售時產生利潤或損失。
其他收入包含存款憑證及銀行帳戶之利息收入，以及出售投資性不動產之 installment payment receivables，與我們於2024年6月與部分非關聯股東所簽訂之某些鎖定期解除協議（"Lock-Up Release Agreements"，"Lock-Up Shares"）相關之收入，以及其他雜項收入，包括印花稅退款。
其他費用包含與企業併購及股份購買協議相關之交易費用，與Lock-Up Release Agreements相關之費用，與New Circle SEPA相關之交易費用，以及其他雜項費用，包括融資成本、洽談交易費用，以及處置不動產之損失。

headings: Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry
利率波動可能提高我們的借款成本，並影響我們不動產投資組合的評價，潛在地影響我們的財務表現與投資回報。
我們的客戶經營業務於哥斯大黎加、哥倫比亞、祕魯與墨西哥特定工業部門。因此，我們的業務運作可能因這些部門經濟衰退而受到不利影響。
競爭增加可能導致租賃率下降與租金收入減少，並可能導致投資機會減少。
我們依賴透過財務市場籌資、資產處分或其他來源，以達成未來成長預期。
我們的負債水平可能影響現金流，並使不動產面臨財產拍賣風險。
規範我們現有負債的協議包含財務及其他契約條件，限制我們追求某些商業機會或採取某些行動的能力。
我們租賃契約中某些條款可能在經營所在地的司法管轄區被視為無法執行，可能限制我們的契約權利與救濟措施。
我們的保險覆蓋範圍可能無法涵蓋所有我們可能面臨的風險。
我們的租戶可能未履行維護所需保險覆蓋的義務，這可能會使我們面臨未投保的財產損壞與責任索賠。
我們投資性不動產的公允價值下降可能對我們的營運成果產生不利影響。
我們面臨與開發新不動產相關的風險，包括因建設成本增加與供應鏈問題所致。
我們可能無法維持、取得或更新，或可能遭遇重大延誤以取得營運所需之政府或其他許可、執照與許可證。
我們的不動產資產可能因公共利益或其他原因而面臨政府徵收與剝奪的風險。
我們可能無法成功執行成長策略，若我們無法取得不動產的收購。

paragraphs: 下列風險因素適用於我們的業務與營運。這些風險因素並非完整列出，投資人被鼓勵針對我們的業務、財務狀況與前景進行自己的研究。您應仔細考慮下列所有風險因素，並與本年度報告中包含或參考的其他資訊一併考量，包括財務資訊。
除了本年度報告中包含的其他資訊，包括「向前看陳述的警示」標題下所提及的內容外，您應仔細考慮下列風險因素，這些風險因素包含重大風險及其他已識別風險，但並非完整列出。其他風險，無論是否目前未知或被認為不重要，或為一般企業所共有的風險，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與現金流產生重大不利影響。
若下列任何風險因素實現，無論是單獨或組合發生，都可能對 LPA 的業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流與未來展望產生重大且不利的影響。這可能會導致普通股的市場價格下跌，並可能導致您的投資部分或全部損失。通常，投資於來自新興市場國家發行人的證券，例如哥斯大黎加、哥倫比亞、祕魯與墨西哥，所承擔的風險與投資於美國發行人證券所承擔的風險有所不同。
我們的業務成功在很大程度上依賴於工業與物流不動產行業的一般經濟狀況與特定市場條件。這些條件的任何不利變化，包括經濟減速或不動產資產價值或租賃活動下降，可能對我們的業務營運、財務狀況、營運結果與未來展望產生重大且不利的影響。
我們的營運結果與財務表現受到工業與物流不動產行業的總體經濟狀況與特定市場動態的重大影響。因此，我們的財務與營運表現、不動產資產價值、收入來源與執行業務策略的能力，可能受到國家與地區經濟狀況變動的影響。

我們所經營的不動產市場表現通常具有週期性，並與美國經濟以及我們所經營國家的經濟狀況，包括哥斯大黎加、哥倫比亞、祕魯與墨西哥，以及投資者對全球經濟展望的觀感有關。名義總體經濟產出（"GDP"）的波動、通貨膨脹增加、利率上升、就業水平下降、投資與經濟活動減少、不動產需求下降、不動產價值下降以及一般經濟減速或衰退時期，或認為這些事件可能發生或正在發生，過去已對不動產市場產生負面影響，並可能對我們的未來表現產生不利影響。此外，我們所經營國家的經濟表現可能取決於或受一個或多個特定產業及其他影響當地經濟的因素所驅動。其他可能影響總體經濟狀況或當地不動產狀況的因素包括：人口與人口結構趨勢、就業與個人收入趨勢、所得與其他稅法、利率變動與融資的可得性與成本、營運成本增加（包括因通貨膨脹及其他因素導致的保險費、公用事業費用與不動產稅，這些費用未必能因租金增加而抵銷）、石油價格變動、建設成本與天氣相關事件。我們根據經濟狀況變動迅速調整投資組合的能力極為有限。
